completed_work: Sorted sage and bitterroot by suitability for a mild calming tincture.
Prepared, steeped, strained, inspected, bottled, and labeled a sage-and-bitterroot calming preparation.
Prepared, inspected, bottled, and labeled a basic healing potion under Master Aloe's supervision and added it to Renn's field kit.
Studied creature body classifications and how physiology changes assessment, treatment suitability, environmental care, topical treatment, and ingestion.
Inspected the finished preparation for appearance, smell, temperature, and sound; no unexpected activity was observed.
Established a comparative chamomile experiment using an ordinary control, slime-processed solids, and a separate pale-gold slime-extracted liquid.
confirmed_discoveries: The slime responds positively to gentle encouragement and praise.
The slime can hold, move, and deliberately release small objects.
The slime placed a pebble inside a vial while holding both.
The slime can gently handle organic material.
The slime remained calmly near chamomile and partially processed it inside its body before stopping voluntarily.
The slime recovered partially changed chamomile and a pale-gold liquid into a vial.
Slime-processed chamomile initially remained physically stable, with softened fragments and finer suspended material than ordinary tea.
A measurable chemical or pH difference from ordinary chamomile tea was observed; its significance is unknown.
The slime can form temporary mossback-like bumps or sprouts as a visual mimicry behavior.
The slime sampled cooled chamomile tea voluntarily and recoiled from hot tea.
The slime deliberately sought Renn and used pinecone mimicry while attempting to lead him toward an injured slime.
A second small blue-green slime is punctured by a jagged point on a larger rusted metal piece buried and wedged between pine roots.
The injured slime is in pain and frightened but did not appear to be rapidly worsening while kept completely still.
Renn and his slime companion are both present beside the injured slime beneath the pine roots.
